author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic records, by its stored name, with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name. It is reachable by its address alone, on one page.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html responds with a page listing every specialty the clinic records, each by its stored name, all on one page with no pagination
under each specialty, every veterinarian holding it is listed by full name, first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
a veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them (PRD edge case 3)
a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it (PRD edge case 4)
specialties appear in name order; veterinarians under each appear by last name, then first name (PRD edge case 5)
the page carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory, as every page must (REQ-SYS-001)
the page's fixed wording is not hard-coded and is present in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002)
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties — NG-2 is unchanged (owner decision, intake line 1)
any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory — deferred to a possible follow-up request (owner decision, intake line 1)
searching or filtering by specialty — NG-9 is unchanged; the page is a full listing that takes no query
a machine-readable form of the specialty directory
translating specialty names — they render as stored
notes: Boundary check: no Non-Goals row changes, so no scope_overrides are needed. NG-2 and NG-9 stand, and REQ-SYS-001 and REQ-LANG-002 bind the new page. No prd-autofix records to audit. Two reversible choices were decided under the narrowest-reading instruction and are recorded here. (1) Order: specialties by name; holders by last name then first name. This matches the name order the veterinarian directory already uses for specialties, and a later slice can amend it cheaply. (2) A specialty no one holds is listed with nothing beneath it, not with a 'none' label. Open questions recorded in PRD § Open Questions: a visible entry point, and a 'none' label for an unheld specialty. docs/prd.md and docs/ubiquitous-language.md were edited in this dispatch: the REQ-VET-003 narrative, acceptance, edge cases 3-5, a Context sentence, two Open Questions, and the Veterinarian directory and Specialty directory terms.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice fits the vet feature package. It uses three In-force catalog patterns (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog), and no new module, integration, or dependency. (1) Repository: new SpecialtyRepository, a read-only Spring Data repository extending Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one findAll-style method. It follows the PetTypeRepository precedent for lookup values. It is required because a specialty no veterinarian holds (edge case 4) cannot be derived from the veterinarians. (2) Value object: new SpecialtyDirectory, an immutable record built by a pure static factory from the specialty list and the veterinarian list. It owns inclusion, the inversion, and both orderings, so the web controller holds no rule (Design Principle 4; Web controller row). It holds names only, never entity references. Its nested records carry the specialty name and each holder's first and last name, with List.copyOf defensive copies. It is not framework-instantiated, so the persistence-entity exception does not apply. (3) Web controller: new package-private SpecialtyController on GET /specialties.html. It reads SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository.findAll() (cached), delegates to SpecialtyDirectory, and renders vets/specialtyList. VetController is left unchanged. Rejected alternative: mapping the inverse association on Specialty. That would give the serialized /vets route a Vet-Specialty-Vet cycle and change an entity the vet directory depends on. Design-doc adjustment: Package Structure vet line, an invariants sentence, Contracts rows (three new, REQ-VET-003 joined on Vet, Specialty, VetRepository), and a new § Scale and Load section with the directory row. Symbols were resolved by grep and file read (the weaker basis; IDE oracle not connected): Vet.getSpecialties sorts by NamedEntity::getName, Specialty declares no equals/hashCode, VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets"), layout.html takes a (template, menu) pair, and messages.properties already defines the keys specialties, vets, name.
integration_points: Binding per entry point: GET /specialties.html binds nothing, with no @RequestParam, no @ModelAttribute, and no path variable. The page takes no query (non-goal: no search or filter, NG-9), and unknown query parameters are ignored. No persisted type is bound (security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries).

Double, repository boundary (SpecialtyDirectoryTests): none. Build real Vet and Specialty instances with set ids, as VetControllerTests already does, and call the static factory directly with no Spring context (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: real objects first). Edge cases 3-5, the omission of a veterinarian holding no specialty, and the first-then-last name pairing are asserted here.

Double, repository boundary (SpecialtyControllerTests): hand-written implementations of VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository, registered through a @TestConfiguration imported by @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class). Both interfaces are narrow Repository extensions, so a hand-written double is a few lines. @MockitoBean is not the sanctioned form for new tests (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: hand-write mocks; the VetControllerTests usage is tolerated precedent, not the pattern).

Double, framework transport: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy). The web tests assert status 200, view name vets/specialtyList, rendered specialty and holder names, no pagination control, and the standard navigation links to /owners/find and /vets.html (REQ-SYS-001).

Layout: the template calls fragments/layout :: layout(~{::body}, 'specialties'). The menu value matches no menu item, so the navigation renders with no item active. No menu item is added (non-goal: reachable by address alone).

Messages (REQ-LANG-002): reuse the existing keys specialties, vets, and name, which are present in every bundle, for the heading and column wording. A new key, if one is needed, goes into messages.properties and every locale bundle in the same change, because I18nPropertiesSyncTest compares bundle keys. Specialty names render as stored and are never translated (non-goal).

patterns.description: Repository for a persisted lookup value; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it but extends the narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer> as VetRepository does, not JpaRepository, keeping the surface minimal (Design Principle 5)
Specialty ordering by Comparator.comparing(NamedEntity::getName); the directory uses the same natural String comparison for specialty order so both directories agree
Constructor-injected repository, package-private controller, view under vets/ (Design Principle 3)
Layout-fragment usage, th:text rendering of names, first-then-last name display

risks.risk: Specialty inherits identity equality, and the specialties reached through each Vet (cached, eager-loaded) are different instances from those SpecialtyRepository returns. Matching by instance or by Set.contains silently drops every holder.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory pairs veterinarians with specialties by persisted id (system-design.md § Contracts invariants sentence). A unit test builds the specialty list and the vets' specialties as distinct instances sharing ids.

risks.risk: Specialty directory path scales with the veterinarian and specialty sets (system-design.md § Scale and Load, specialty directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form, per the row: load both sets whole, group in memory by specialty id, sort. No paging, no custom query, no new cache.

risks.risk: Ordering ties: two holders with identical last and first names, or two specialties with the same stored name (the name column is indexed, not unique), render in arbitrary order. That breaches the stable-order intent of edge case 1 and edge case 5.
risks.mitigation: Break ties by persisted id after the name keys so the order is deterministic. The PRD keys (specialty name; last name, then first name) stay primary.

risks.risk: Stored veterinarian and specialty names are echoed into HTML (system-design.md § Threat Model, cross-site scripting row).
risks.mitigation: Render every name with th:text, never th:utext; Thymeleaf escaping is the control.

risks.risk: Veterinarians come from the unevicted vet cache while specialties are read fresh. An out-of-band data change can show a new specialty with stale holders (system-design.md § Open Questions from the Survey, item 5).
risks.mitigation: Accepted as-is; the application has no write path for either set. Do not add a cache or eviction in this slice.

risks.risk: A data-access failure reaches the error page, which renders the exception message (system-design.md § Known Defects, REQ-SYS-002 row).
risks.mitigation: Errors flow outward unchanged (architecture-principles.md § Domain Core); the existing defect is not fixed or worsened here.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. No ADR: every type matches an In-force catalog pattern, and the rejected inverse-mapping alternative is contained to this slice. The doctor passes (0 failures). Open questions left to the owner, not decided here: (1) a visible entry point and (2) a 'none' label under an unheld specialty (both already in PRD § Open Questions); (3) the realistic veterinarian and specialty counts, recorded as unrecorded and treated as bounded in § Scale and Load. Id tie-breaking is the narrowest deterministic reading of edge cases 1 and 5 and is cheap to revise. VetRepository.findAll() now has a real consumer beyond the machine-readable route listed under Known Defects, so removing that route later must keep findAll(). Native image: no new entity is added. If a native build fails on Thymeleaf reading the SpecialtyDirectory record accessors, a reflection hint in PetClinicRuntimeHints is the remedy. The JVM test suite cannot observe this (tests are @DisabledInNativeImage).
